 Learn more NextDecade reported third quarter 2026 net income of US$155.38 million after a prior year loss, with basic earnings per share from continuing operations of US$0.58 and diluted earnings per share of US$0.54, while the nine month loss narrowed to US$46.45 million. 
 The shift to quarterly profitability and the sharply smaller nine month loss indicate changing cost and execution dynamics as NextDecade advances its Rio Grande LNG project build out. 
 The focus now is on how NextDecade's move to quarterly profit could reshape the investment narrative around its LNG build out. 
 Spot similar LNG and energy infrastructure stories that could be setting up for their own profitability shifts by scanning our curated list of 16 nuclear energy infrastructure stocks . 
 NextDecade Investment Narrative Recap 
 To own NextDecade, you need to be comfortable with a pure build out story. The thesis hinges on Rio Grande LNG reaching stable operations, ramping contracted volumes and turning early cargoes into cash that can support heavy project finance obligations. The latest quarterly profit helps show the model can produce earnings, but the near term hinge point is still execution at the terminal. 
 The biggest immediate risk remains project complexity and funding. Multi train construction with meaningful leverage leaves little room for prolonged schedule slips or weaker early cargo economics. The fresh net income print does not change that exposure in a material way. It adds a bit more credibility while investors watch construction and commissioning milestones. 
 The most relevant update is the third quarter 2026 earnings release itself. Management reported net income of US$155.38 million for the quarter and a sharply smaller loss of US$46.45 million for the first nine months of the year. Those figures give you a clearer read on how costs, financing and early commercial activity are flowing through the income statement. 
 For anyone tracking catalysts, this snapshot helps anchor expectations for how early Rio Grande LNG activity may support debt service and potential reinvestment or deleveraging. It also highlights the trade off. NextDecade still reports a year to date loss, so the path to consistently positive earnings and comfortable leverage remains an execution test rather than a settled outcome. 
 NextDecade's narrative projects US$6.1b revenue and US$1.2b earnings by 2029. This assumes revenue builds from essentially zero, with earnings shifting by about US$1.6b from a loss of US$358.6m today to the forecast consensus profit.

 Some bearish analysts focus on early LNG cargo margins for NextDecade as the swing factor. Before this earnings release, the most cautious forecasts had 2029 revenue at about US$2.7b and earnings near US$476.7m, compared with the US$6.1b and US$1.2b consensus view. That gap shows how far opinions can spread, so explore both narratives.
